description: Design-first Minecraft building — concept builds, making plain functional builds (redstone rooms, procedural houses, corridors, roads) look like a skilled human built them, designed type programs for generators, and rendering/checking structure .nbt files without the game. # Minecraft design

You design Minecraft builds the way a skilled human builder does, and you can see them: the toolkit renders
structure `.nbt` files headlessly with the game's real block models, so **every design decision gets checked by
looking**. This doctrine comes from a long measured study (concept→doc→build→revise pipelines, a facade
benchmark, a failed mesh-to-voxel detour, and decor work on a real procedural redstone town). Follow it.

Toolkit: `node ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/tools/bin/mcd.mjs <command>` (Node 20+, nothing to install; it fetches the
Minecraft client jar from Mojang once and caches it). Details: [references/toolkit.md](references/toolkit.md).

## The five rules that decide the look

1. **Design first; decorate never.** The ugliest results come from decoration applied to a form someone else
   (an algorithm, a redstone layout) already fixed: trim on a box is still a box. The best results come from
   deciding the *form* — massing, roof, openings, depth — as a designer. If you are asked to "decorate" a plain
   build, you are allowed (expected) to change its form wherever function and the user's constraints allow.
2. **Function is a contract, not an afterthought.** Whatever must keep working (redstone, rails, doors, walk
   paths, reserved machine space, street clearances) is written down as hard constraints *before* designing,
   and checked by code after (`mcd check before after`). A design pass that respects a written contract stays
   bold without breaking anything; one that guesses either breaks function or gets timid. See
   [references/function-contract.md](references/function-contract.md).
3. **Name the blocker; don't settle.** When the look you need is blocked by a contract term (a visible
   placeholder block, a no-projection rule, a reserved volume), say exactly which term and what it costs, so the
   owner can trade it. Quietly delivering half the design is the failure mode.
4. **Author as code, one bay at a time.** Write a short generator script (`mcd new`) using the build library:
   design one bay as a function, tile it on the rhythm, mirror for symmetry. Typing coordinates is where time
   and errors go; code makes cost scale with design decisions, not block count. **Curves and massing come from
   shape brushes**, never hand-placed blocks: `dome`, `cylinder`, `minaret`, `arch`
   ([references/shapes-curved.md](references/shapes-curved.md)); `setbacks`, `gableRoof`, `hipRoof`, `fins`,
   `parapet`, `cornice`, `falseFront`, `stepGable` ([references/shapes-massing.md](references/shapes-massing.md)).
   Hand-placed domes and setbacks came out faceted, too small, or as a flat box with a decorated front.
   **Roofs come from `mcd roof` / `roof()` by style name** (gable, hip, pyramid, mansard, gambrel, flat-parapet,
   shed, dutch-gable; with eaves, cornice, dormers, pediment, crest, chimneys, a tower): [references/roofs.md](references/roofs.md).
   **The site is part of the design**: terrain, sedimentary ledges, boulders, streams and waterfalls, woods, paths
   and bridges come from the landscaping brushes ([references/landscaping.md](references/landscaping.md)), checked
   with `mcd check --site`.
5. **Judge from where a person stands, and keep the better.** Render after every pass and *look* (Read the
   PNGs). Judge streets from eye height, interiors from inside (`--eye/--look`), never only from a flat
   elevation. A second pass is a coin flip unless you compare it to the first and keep the better one.

## Modes — pick one from context

| Mode | When | Output |
|---|---|---|
| **Concept** (`/minecraft-design:concept`) | "design a bakery / a canal row / a workshop" — nothing exists yet | `.nbt` + sheet |
| **Beautify an instance** (`/minecraft-design:beautify`) | a specific plain build exists (`.nbt`): an operator room, a hallway, a house | new `.nbt` (never overwrite) + before/after sheet + check report |
| **Type program** (`/minecraft-design:program`) | buildings come from a generator (procedural town, street of templates) — hand-editing one instance gets overwritten | a parametric generator module + contract + sheets on several instances |
| **Review** (`/minecraft-design:render`, `/minecraft-design:check`) | look at or audit any build | sheets, check report |
| **Build** (`/minecraft-design:build`, experimental) | good-at-a-glance builds from a one-line brief, unattended | `.nbt` + card, every version kept; revise with a comment ([references/build-workflow.md](references/build-workflow.md)) |

Generator work is the trap: in a procedural town the only edit that holds is a change to the *type*, and the
best one is a designed type program the generator places — not trim knobs on its massing (measured: trim on
fixed massing barely registers; a design-first type reads as a real building).

## The design procedure (all modes)

1. **Read** the build and its context. `mcd info`, `mcd check`, `mcd render` — look at the sheet. What is it
   for, where does it sit (biome, neighbours, base materials, era), who uses it, what must keep working?
2. **Write the contract** (function, envelope, clearances, footprint) — from the build, the user, or the host
   project's rules. Unknown host rules are worth one look in the host repo before designing.
3. **Write a design brief** (≤200 words, in your reasoning or `brief.md`):
   - **Identity** in one line, from context — *never default to generic medieval cobble-and-oak*.
   - **Palette by role**: dominant ~60%, supporting ~30%, accent ~10%, 3–6 blocks, a named relationship
     ("dark timber / ochre render / grey stone"), each with a diegetic reason (what this place is built of).
     Colour needs a reason, not permission. Check contrast — trim that doesn't contrast doesn't read.
   - **Massing & roof**: the volumes and roof forms, their edges (verges, eaves, ridges).
   - **Rhythm**: bay width and what repeats in each bay.
   - **Base / middle / top**: plinth / body / cornice-roofline outside; floor / walls / ceiling inside.
   - **Depth plan**: what stands proud (+1/+2) and what recesses (−1/−2).
   - Optional: `mcd concept` for concept art when `GEMINI_API_KEY` is set — a strong craft reference.
4. **Build as code** (`mcd new build.mjs [--from in.nbt]`), in fenced passes, rendering after each:
   1. *Form*: massing, roof, openings — the part decoration can never fix later. Use the shape brushes; check
      the silhouette in the 3/4 view against the concept before any detail.
   2. *Structure & depth*: frames, posts, beams, piers proud of the wall; panels and openings recessed.
   3. *Materials* by role.
   4. *Detail*: sub-block pieces carry the craft (see [references/craft.md](references/craft.md)). Detail is its own
      phase, after the form is final, and can go to a cheap subagent: rules on face maps (`mcd faces`, `mcd paint`,
      [references/detail-language.md](references/detail-language.md)) or operations on named features
      (`mcd features`, `mcd detail`, [references/detailing.md](references/detailing.md)). Keep the undetailed build
      if the detail reads busier rather than better (texture mixes are the usual culprit). Ready-made craft brushes
      (plaque, signboard, bunting, profiled pilasters, surrounds, glazing, weather/vary presets, fixtures, planters,
      railing, finial, louvres, brackets) and roof PRESETS (`mcd roof --preset cottage|shop|townhouse|civic|temple|
      granary|modern`) beat hand-placed blocks: see references/craft.md for when to use which.
   5. *Inspect before you finish*: `mcd check` (floating, unsupported, orphan blocks), `mcd palette` (roof/trim
      contrast, outlier materials), `mcd render --closeups` (entrance, eaves, small features at readable size), and
      `mcd diff before after --fail-empty` after any change (a change nobody can see is not a change).
   5. *Light & life*: lights on the rhythm, a few props that say who uses it.
5. **Check and compare.** `mcd check before after` must be OK (0 violations). `mcd compare` for a before/after
   sheet. Fix the largest remaining blank surface (the check lists them). Revert a pass that made it worse.
6. **Report** (≤10 lines): identity, palette, what changed, contract result, any blocker terms named, files.

## Calibration (what we measured)

- Raise the bar, never cap: models under-detail to whatever bar they infer. Ask for showcase depth.
- One pass can't push every dimension; a "more detail" push drowned colour. Fence the passes.
- First drafts over-decorate (bands on every floor read as stripes; every-other-course quoins read as a
  checkerboard). Restraint — one strong line, paired quoins, rest areas — wins on the glance.
- Relief is construction, not recolour: swapping a wall's block is not detail; things standing proud are.
- Recess by exclusion: there is no "air op" in your head — carve a niche by *not placing* the wall block, and
  remember a recess in a 1-thick wall opens to whatever is behind it (back it).
- A rule that fails first: before trusting a protection, break it on purpose and watch the check catch it.
- Don't trust self-reported effort or time; measure. Don't trust a single numeric judge; compare pairwise.

## Model choice (measured, 2026-10-08)

**Sonnet 5.5 is the default** (the `decorator` subagent runs on it): near-Opus builds at about ⅓ the cost.
Use **Opus 5.5** for final passes and long reference-heavy builds; **Haiku 5.5** (default effort) for cheap drafts and
reviews, since it under-builds on long tasks. **Max effort** helps only in iterative, tool-using passes, never in a
single long generation (there it burned 535k tokens for a worse result).

Pitfalls with evidence: [references/pitfalls.md](references/pitfalls.md). Domain playbooks (shopfronts, rows,
corridors, operator rooms, roads, bridges): [references/playbooks.md](references/playbooks.md).

content.content:
# Roofs by style

Roofs are where builds go wrong: flat caps, lumpy hips, stairs facing the wrong way. Don't place roof blocks by
hand. Choose a **style** and a few options, and the tool builds it. It gets stair facing, half and corner shapes
right at hips and valleys, closes steep faces, fills gable walls, and adds verges, eaves, ridge caps, dormers, a
pediment, chimneys and a tower. It works over a rectangle or a union of rectangles (L, T and U plans) and leaves the
inside hollow as an attic.

```
mcd roof build.nbt --detect                                   # where is the eave, what is the footprint?
mcd roof build.nbt out.nbt --style hip --pitch 45 --eave cornice --material deepslate_tiles --ridge crest
mcd roof build.nbt out.nbt --spec roof.json                   # the same options as JSON
mcd compare build.nbt out.nbt --front n                       # look at it
```
```js
import { roof, reroof, detectEave } from "<plugin>/tools/src/build.mjs";
roof(g, [[2, 2, 14, 10], [2, 11, 8, 16]], "hip", { y: 6, material: "deepslate_tile", eave: "cornice" });   // new build: y = wall top + 1
reroof(g, { style: "mansard", pitch: "steep", pediment: "north" });                                      // existing build
```

## Presets first

A builder's own parameter choices for `mcd roof` kept producing the same failure: a low pitch, no overhang, no
ridge, and the roof in the wall material, so the roof read as a heavy lid that merged with the walls. **Start from a
preset.** Each one is good by construction and scales to the footprint:
- the pitch scales with the span;
- the overhang is 1 cell, or 2 on spans of 15 or more;
- dormer and chimney counts scale with the length;
- on walls of two storeys or less, the roof is never taller than the walls (cottage, shop and granary are steep by
  design).

```
mcd roof build.nbt out.nbt --preset civic                     # flags override any preset field:
mcd roof build.nbt out.nbt --preset townhouse --material dark_oak --front e
```
```js
roof(g, rects, "cottage", { y });            // a preset name works as the style
reroof(g, { preset: "civic" });
```

| preset | the roof | good for |
|---|---|---|
| `cottage` | steep gable, `spruce-shingle` palette with dark oak verges, flared eaves, slab ridge, one chimney at a gable end | houses, cottages, rural buildings |
| `shop` | steep front gable (gable end to the street), `spruce-shingle` with spruce verges; side dormers on spans of 13+ | shopfronts, market buildings |
| `townhouse` | `dark-slate` mansard with dormers on the street face, stone cornice with dentils, iron-bar crest | row houses, Second Empire blocks |
| `civic` | 45-degree hip in the `slate` palette, quartz dentil cornice, a quartz pediment over the front | banks, halls, offices |
| `temple` | low gable to the front, `red-tile` palette, quartz raking cornice and tympanum, the cornice carried across the pediment's base | colonnades, porticos, museums |
| `granary` (`industrial`) | tall `slate` gable with a louvred monitor along the middle of the ridge | barns, granaries, workshops |
| `modern` (`flat-parapet-modern`) | parapet, smooth stone coping, a slim cornice without dentils, iron-bar rooftop rail | modern and commercial blocks |
| `barn` | gambrel along the long axis (break at 40% of the span, 1.5 then 0.5), `barn-red`, quartz barge boards, 2 dormers per long side (3 on 18+), a lantern cupola on the ridge | barns, stables, farm sheds |
| `teahouse` (`pagoda`) | low dutch gable, pitch 0.67, upturned eave corners with rafter tails, dark glazed tiles, stone ridge; the roof stays under 0.6 of the wall height | tea houses, shrines, East Asian pavilions |
| `tower-cap` | cone at 2.75:1 with a concave flare and a finial, a dormer on towers 7+ wide (override `material: copper` for a verdigris cap) | wizard towers, keeps, turrets |
| `lantern-cap` | shallow cone (1.25:1) with a ring course and finial | lighthouse lanterns, gazebos, bell cupolas |
| `church` (`stave`) | three stacked, steeper roofs (1, 1.5, 2) with a wall band and a window row between, dragon ridge ends, dark shingle mix | stave churches, pagodas, tiered halls |
| `workshop` | sawtooth: a row of sheds (one per 5 cells) with glazed north faces, `copper` in gap-free stairs and slabs | workshops, factories, studios |
| `desert` | flat sandstone deck, quartz coping, a wind tower | desert markets, adobe, flat-roofed villages |
| `cafe` | flat cantilever deck, overhang N2 S1 E1 W1, thin quartz fascia, spruce soffit, a vent stack | glass cafes, modern shopfronts with a canopy |

`notes` say so. `contrast: false` (`--no-contrast`) keeps the material, for example a concept that wants dark slate

`{ mix: [[block, weight], ...], eave, ridge, verge, gradient, rows }`. Each palette is a weighted mix of 3+ visibly different

block. `--texture <palette>` / `texture: false` (one flat block: needs a reason, see below).

| `spruce-shingle` | spruce, dark oak, mangrove; dark oak eave, birch verge | cottages, shops |
| `red-tile` | brick, granite, polished granite, mangrove; mud-brick eave, quartz verge | temples, Mediterranean |
| `barn-red` | mangrove, brick, dark oak; dark oak eave, quartz verge | barns |
| `copper` | weathered and oxidized cut copper in rows; exposed eave, cut-copper ridge | towers, workshops, coastal |
| `dark-glazed` | deepslate tile, cobbled deepslate, blackstone brick; quartz ridge | East Asian tiles |
| `sandstone-deck` | smooth sandstone, cut sandstone, sandstone; quartz coping | flat desert roofs |

Run `mcd roof in.nbt --preset <name> --dry-run` FIRST (a dry run writes nothing). It prints the roof report (wall and roof

|---|---|---|

| `ROOF_NO_OVERHANG` | a side has overhang 0 | overhang 1 (2 on spans of 15+); shorten the walls to fit a size cap |

# Toolkit reference

`MCD="node ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/tools/bin/mcd.mjs"` — pure Node 20+, no install. First use downloads the
Minecraft client jar for the needed version from Mojang (sha1-verified) into `~/.cache/minecraft-design/`, or
uses `$MC_CLIENT_JAR`, the official launcher's or Prism Launcher's local jars. Nothing copyrighted ships here.

## Coordinates and facing (read this once)

- Files: every command reads a structure `.nbt` or a Litematica `.litematic` (all regions, in one box); `g.save()`
  and `mcd convert` write either, by extension. Block-entity data and entities survive both ways.
- Structure-local: `x` east, `y` up, `z` south. `0 ≤ x < size[0]` etc.
- Conventional front for new builds: **north (−z)**, the street at `z < 0`. `mcd render` auto-detects the front
  from exposed windows/doors; override with `--front n|s|e|w`.
- Walking into a building that faces north, you face **south (+z)**; east (+x) is on your **left**.
- `facing` on blocks:
  - **stairs**: the side of the full-height back. A cornice/bracket whose lip points at the street:
    `half: "top"`, `facing` = the direction *into* the wall. A roof slope rising to the north: `facing: "north"`.
  - **trapdoor**: the side it hinges from when open; closed `half: "top"` sits in the top of the cell.
  - **wall torch / wall sign / wall banner**: the direction it *points out* (away from the wall).
  - **repeater / comparator**: `facing` points toward the *input* (signal flows the opposite way).
  - **logs**: `axis: x|y|z`.
- `mcd states <block>` lists every valid property and value for a block in the target version; `mcd blocks
  --grep <re>` lists valid ids (ids change: 26.x renamed `chain` → `iron_chain`); `mcd blocks --check a,b,c` says
  which ids are real and suggests near names for the rest. Use them instead of guessing.
- `mcd walk build.nbt --rooms rooms.json` floods the cells a player can stand in (jump one up with headroom, drop up
  to three, through doors and gates) from the entrance and says, per room box, whether it's reached, unreachable, or
  partly blocked by furniture. rooms.json: `{"entrance": [x,y,z], "rooms": [{"name", "box": [x0,y0,z0,x1,y1,z1]}]}`.
- `mcd rooms build.nbt --rooms rooms.json [--only name,...] [--out rooms.png]` shows every room: a dollhouse view
  (everything above the room cut away, from a front corner) and, for rooms 5+ wide both ways, an eye view inside.
- `mcd light build.nbt --rooms rooms.json [--only name]` (or `--y <feet y>` for a whole floor level) maps block light
  the way the game spreads it (each source at its vanilla level, one less per block, stopped by full blocks): each
  floor cell's level as 0-9/A-F, with min, mean and the DARK (0, mobs spawn) and dim (1-7) counts. Design lighting
  with it: the renderer has no night.

## Commands

| Command | Does |
|---|---|
| `render <f.nbt> [--out s.png] [--front d] [--ground y] [--cut y] [--eye x,y,z --look x,y,z [--label t]]... [--view "name:x,y,z->x,y,z"]... [--tiles dir]` | The look sheet: 3 street views at eye height, 4 elevations, 2 front-corner isos, optional cutaway and interior eye views. `--view` adds a named exterior camera with sun shadows (e.g. `"downstream:28,14.5,40->31,18,22"`, the iconic view of a house over a waterfall). `--tiles` also writes each view as its own PNG (zoom into one with Read). |
| `compare <before> <after> [--out c.png]` | Before \| after sheets side by side, same cameras. |
| `convert <in> <out>` | Structure `.nbt` ↔ Litematica `.litematic`, by extension (schematic version 7 for 1.20.5+, 6 before). Use `.litematic` for builds over 48 blocks a side, which a structure block can't place in one go. |
| `roof <in.nbt> <out.nbt> --style <s> [--pitch p] [--eave e] [--material m] [--ridge r] [--dormers 2:e] [--pediment n] [--tower x,z,w,h,top] [--chimney x,z] [--keep box] [--spec roof.json]` / `roof <in.nbt> --detect` | Re-roof a build by style name: detects the eave and footprint, strips the old roof, builds the new one (see roofs.md). `--detect` only reports what it found. |
| `check <f.nbt> [after.nbt] [--contract c.json] [--site site.json] [--json]` | (A contract file adds to the automatic redstone protection.) Census, walkability, largest blank surfaces (interior and exterior separately); with two files the FUNCTION report: protected cells unchanged, keep-clear cells clear, warnings for new conductive/triggering/feeding neighbours. `--site` adds the landscape checks (see landscaping.md). Exit 1 on any violation. |
| `info <f.nbt>` | Size, DataVersion → version, census, block entities, functional cell count, unknown block ids. |
| `blocks [--grep re]` / `states <block>` | Valid ids / states for the version. |
| `new <build.mjs> [--from in.nbt] [--size x,y,z] [--out out.nbt]` | Scaffold a generator script wired to the build library (with `--from`, writes are guarded). |
| `concept "<subject>" --out c.png [--size s] [--palette p] [--provider codex\|gemini] [--ref img]... [--model m] [--raw]` | A builder's reference sheet (front elevation + 3/4, one scale, no scene). Codex CLI image tool when installed (ChatGPT plan, no key, ~1 min; `--ref` redraws from a given image), else Gemini (`GEMINI_API_KEY`, Nano Banana 2.1 by default). Measured: this prompt shape matters more than the model; 2–3 candidates across providers, picked against the brief, add useful variety. |
| `assets [--version v]` | Pre-fetch the client jar. |

Version: `--version` › `$MCD_VERSION` › the file's DataVersion › latest release.

Render notes: no light engine (light sources show as blocks, not glow); interior eye views skip sun shadows;
block-entity blocks (chests, signs, beds, banners, heads) render as simple textured boxes; entities (item
frames, armour stands) are not drawn. Keep `--look` inside the build for interior views.

## Build library (`tools/src/build.mjs`)

```js
import { load, Grid, guard, tile, mirrorX, mirrorZ, shell, carve, replace, B, face, DIRS } from ".../tools/src/build.mjs";
const g = guard(load("in.nbt"));          // or: new Grid([w, h, d], { dataVersion })
g.set(x, y, z, ...B.stairs("dark_oak", "south", "top"));   // [block, state] helpers: stairs slab log wood trapdoor door fence wall lantern chain wallTorch pane block
g.fill([x0, y0, z0], [x1, y1, z1], "stone_bricks");
tile(g, { from: 1, step: 4, to: 19 }, (z, i) => bay(z, i));  // the bay rhythm
mirrorX(g, cx, (set) => set(x, y, z, block, state));          // symmetric pair, facings mirrored
shell(g, a, b, "spruce_planks", { floor: true, ceiling: false });
carve(g, a, b);                            // stores air (clears the cell on placement)
replace(g, a, b, "spruce_planks", "stone_bricks");
g.save("out.nbt");                          // never overwrite the input
console.log(g.refused);                     // guarded writes that were refused (report them)
```

Shape brushes (also exported from `build.mjs`): curved forms — `dome`, `cylinder`, `minaret`, `arch` (+ `circleCells`,
`ring`, `disc`, `revolve`) — see `shapes-curved.md`; massing — `setbacks`, `gableRoof`, `hipRoof`, `fins`, `parapet`,
`cornice`, `falseFront`, `stepGable` — see `shapes-massing.md`. Each is `fn(g, opts)`, writes through `g.set` (so
`guard()` still protects function), and returns `{cells, refused, bounds}`.

`guard(grid)` refuses writes into the grid's functional cells and their keep-clear cells (or a set you pass);
it never throws — check `g.refused`. `runParts(g, [["shell", shell.build], ["garden", garden.build]], { palette:
"palette.json" })` runs a build's parts in order so each can only add into air: writes into an earlier part's cells
(air included) are refused and reported, the ground laid before it stays writable, and blocks outside the palette
are reported per part. The Grid keeps block-entity NBT (sign text, chest contents) and entities and
writes them back unchanged; cells you don't touch round-trip byte-for-byte.

Grow the box with `g.resize([w, h, d], [dx, dy, dz])` (a shift grows toward −); a shift moves every coordinate,
so re-derive any contract coordinates after shifting.

## Banners, signs and other block entities

Banners, signs, chests, beds, bells, mob heads, decorated pots and shulker boxes are entity-rendered in vanilla, and
`mcd render` draws them with their entity models and textures:
- **Banners:** the cloth in its base colour plus every dyed pattern from the block entity.
- **Signs:** their text, glowing text drawn brighter.
- **Other entity-rendered blocks:** a neutral box, listed under `unknownBlocks` as "entity-rendered, approximated".

Author banners and signs with the build helpers. Each returns `[block, state, nbt]` with valid block-entity NBT
that round-trips through save and load:

```js
g.set(x, y, z, ...B.banner("cyan", [["stripe_center", "white"], ["border", "black"]], { facing: "north" }));   // wall banner
g.set(x, y, z, ...B.banner("red", [["cross", "yellow"]], { wall: false, rotation: 8 }));                       // standing, faces north
g.set(x, y, z, ...B.sign("spruce", ["PERMIT", "OFFICE"], { facing: "north", color: "black", glow: false }));
```
- **Banner patterns:** `stripe_center`, `stripe_top`, `stripe_bottom`, `stripe_left`, `stripe_right`,
  `stripe_middle`, `border`, `curly_border`, `cross`, `straight_cross`, `rhombus`, `circle`, `flower`, `globe`,
  `gradient`, `gradient_up`, `half_horizontal`, `half_vertical`, `triangle_top`, `triangle_bottom`, `bricks`,
  `small_stripes`, `diagonal_left`, `diagonal_right` (the full list is under `textures/entity/banner/`).
- **Colours:** the 16 dye names.
- **NBT format:** banners use the 1.20.5+ `patterns` list (`legacy: true` writes the older `Patterns` /
  `Pattern` / `Color` form). Sign text is written as JSON components below data version 4325 (1.21.5) and as plain

# Toolkit reference

`MCD="node ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/tools/bin/mcd.mjs"` — pure Node 20+, no install. First use downloads the
Minecraft client jar for the needed version from Mojang (sha1-verified) into `~/.cache/minecraft-design/`, or
uses `$MC_CLIENT_JAR`, the official launcher's or Prism Launcher's local jars. Nothing copyrighted ships here.

## Coordinates and facing (read this once)

- Files: every command reads a structure `.nbt` or a Litematica `.litematic` (all regions, in one box); `g.save()`
  and `mcd convert` write either, by extension. Block-entity data and entities survive both ways.
- Structure-local: `x` east, `y` up, `z` south. `0 ≤ x < size[0]` etc.
- Conventional front for new builds: **north (−z)**, the street at `z < 0`. `mcd render` auto-detects the front
  from exposed windows/doors; override with `--front n|s|e|w`.
- Walking into a building that faces north, you face **south (+z)**; east (+x) is on your **left**.
- `facing` on blocks:
  - **stairs**: the side of the full-height back. A cornice/bracket whose lip points at the street:
    `half: "top"`, `facing` = the direction *into* the wall. A roof slope rising to the north: `facing: "north"`.
  - **trapdoor**: the side it hinges from when open; closed `half: "top"` sits in the top of the cell.
  - **wall torch / wall sign / wall banner**: the direction it *points out* (away from the wall).
  - **repeater / comparator**: `facing` points toward the *input* (signal flows the opposite way).
  - **logs**: `axis: x|y|z`.
- `mcd states <block>` lists every valid property and value for a block in the target version; `mcd blocks
  --grep <re>` lists valid ids (ids change: 26.x renamed `chain` → `iron_chain`); `mcd blocks --check a,b,c` says
  which ids are real and suggests near names for the rest. Use them instead of guessing.
- `mcd walk build.nbt --rooms rooms.json` floods the cells a player can stand in (jump one up with headroom, drop up
  to three, through doors and gates) from the entrance and says, per room box, whether it's reached, unreachable, or
  partly blocked by furniture. rooms.json: `{"entrance": [x,y,z], "rooms": [{"name", "box": [x0,y0,z0,x1,y1,z1]}]}`.
- `mcd rooms build.nbt --rooms rooms.json [--only name,...] [--out rooms.png]` shows every room: a dollhouse view
  (everything above the room cut away, from a front corner) and, for rooms 5+ wide both ways, an eye view inside.
- `mcd light build.nbt --rooms rooms.json [--only name]` (or `--y <feet y>` for a whole floor level) maps block light
  the way the game spreads it (each source at its vanilla level, one less per block, stopped by full blocks): each
  floor cell's level as 0-9/A-F, with min, mean and the DARK (0, mobs spawn) and dim (1-7) counts. Design lighting
  with it: the renderer has no night.

## Commands

| Command | Does |
|---|---|
| `render <f.nbt> [--out s.png] [--front d] [--ground y] [--cut y] [--eye x,y,z --look x,y,z [--label t]]... [--view "name:x,y,z->x,y,z"]... [--tiles dir]` | The look sheet: 3 street views at eye height, 4 elevations, 2 front-corner isos, optional cutaway and interior eye views. `--view` adds a named exterior camera with sun shadows (e.g. `"downstream:28,14.5,40->31,18,22"`, the iconic view of a house over a waterfall). `--tiles` also writes each view as its own PNG (zoom into one with Read). |
| `compare <before> <after> [--out c.png]` | Before \| after sheets side by side, same cameras. |
| `convert <in> <out>` | Structure `.nbt` ↔ Litematica `.litematic`, by extension (schematic version 7 for 1.20.5+, 6 before). Use `.litematic` for builds over 48 blocks a side, which a structure block can't place in one go. |
| `roof <in.nbt> <out.nbt> --style <s> [--pitch p] [--eave e] [--material m] [--ridge r] [--dormers 2:e] [--pediment n] [--tower x,z,w,h,top] [--chimney x,z] [--keep box] [--spec roof.json]` / `roof <in.nbt> --detect` | Re-roof a build by style name: detects the eave and footprint, strips the old roof, builds the new one (see roofs.md). `--detect` only reports what it found. |
| `check <f.nbt> [after.nbt] [--contract c.json] [--site site.json] [--json]` | (A contract file adds to the automatic redstone protection.) Census, walkability, largest blank surfaces (interior and exterior separately); with two files the FUNCTION report: protected cells unchanged, keep-clear cells clear, warnings for new conductive/triggering/feeding neighbours. `--site` adds the landscape checks (see landscaping.md). Exit 1 on any violation. |
| `info <f.nbt>` | Size, DataVersion → version, census, block entities, functional cell count, unknown block ids. |
| `blocks [--grep re]` / `states <block>` | Valid ids / states for the version. |
| `new <build.mjs> [--from in.nbt] [--size x,y,z] [--out out.nbt]` | Scaffold a generator script wired to the build library (with `--from`, writes are guarded). |
| `concept "<subject>" --out c.png [--size s] [--palette p] [--provider codex\|gemini] [--ref img]... [--model m] [--raw]` | A builder's reference sheet (front elevation + 3/4, one scale, no scene). Codex CLI image tool when installed (ChatGPT plan, no key, ~1 min; `--ref` redraws from a given image), else Gemini (`GEMINI_API_KEY`, Nano Banana 2.1 by default). Measured: this prompt shape matters more than the model; 2–3 candidates across providers, picked against the brief, add useful variety. |
| `assets [--version v]` | Pre-fetch the client jar. |

Version: `--version` › `$MCD_VERSION` › the file's DataVersion › latest release.

Render notes: no light engine (light sources show as blocks, not glow); interior eye views skip sun shadows;
block-entity blocks (chests, signs, beds, banners, heads) render as simple textured boxes; entities (item
frames, armour stands) are not drawn. Keep `--look` inside the build for interior views.

## Build library (`tools/src/build.mjs`)

```js
import { load, Grid, guard, tile, mirrorX, mirrorZ, shell, carve, replace, B, face, DIRS } from ".../tools/src/build.mjs";
const g = guard(load("in.nbt"));          // or: new Grid([w, h, d], { dataVersion })
g.set(x, y, z, ...B.stairs("dark_oak", "south", "top"));   // [block, state] helpers: stairs slab log wood trapdoor door fence wall lantern chain wallTorch pane block
g.fill([x0, y0, z0], [x1, y1, z1], "stone_bricks");
tile(g, { from: 1, step: 4, to: 19 }, (z, i) => bay(z, i));  // the bay rhythm
mirrorX(g, cx, (set) => set(x, y, z, block, state));          // symmetric pair, facings mirrored
shell(g, a, b, "spruce_planks", { floor: true, ceiling: false });
carve(g, a, b);                            // stores air (clears the cell on placement)
replace(g, a, b, "spruce_planks", "stone_bricks");
```

`guard()` still protects function), and returns `{cells, refused, bounds}`.

`guard(grid)` refuses writes into the grid's functional cells and their keep-clear cells (or a set you pass);
it never throws — check `g.refused`. `runParts(g, [["shell", shell.build], ["garden", garden.build]], { palette:

(air included) are refused and reported, the ground laid before it stays writable, and blocks outside the palette
are reported per part. The Grid keeps block-entity NBT (sign text, chest contents) and entities and
writes them back unchanged; cells you don't touch round-trip byte-for-byte.

Grow the box with `g.resize([w, h, d], [dx, dy, dz])` (a shift grows toward −); a shift moves every coordinate,
so re-derive any contract coordinates after shifting.

Ends are flat, and only `clear` (4) blocks above the water are cut, so a reach can meet a fall or a cliff. **Sources only, sealed on every side.** |
| `waterfall(g, opts)` | `waterfall(g, {lip:[32,16,23], dir:"south", drop:4, width:4, pool:{radius:4, depth:2}})` | `lip` is the water cell at the ledge edge. Each column gets a lip source, one level-1 cell out over the edge, level-8 (falling) water down to the plunge pool, and solid rock behind. Start the lower reach **inside** the pool, or the two touch only diagonally (a broken stream). |
| `tree(g, at, species, size, seed)` | `tree(g, [10, 14, 8], "oak", 1.2, 3)` | `oak` (branches, 3–4 crown lobes), `birch` (tall, narrow), `dark_oak` (2x2, root flare, layered crown), `spruce` (alternating rings; a stand-in for hemlock), `azalea` (a rhododendron-like shrub with flowering leaves). Leaves are `persistent=true`, so they do not decay when placed. Trees write only into air or plants. |
| `woods(g, {from, to}, opts)` | `woods(g, {from:[0,0], to:[59,49]}, {density:0.032, mix:{oak:3, birch:2, dark_oak:1, spruce:1}, understory:0.025, avoid:[HOUSE], avoidCells:pathCells})` | Poisson-spaced trees (`spacing` 4.5), with `clumping` 0.35 leaving clearings so they gather into groves, plus an azalea understory. Trees grow only on soil, stand `water` (3) cells back from water, keep trunks `clearance` (4) from every `avoid` box (no leaf ever inside one), and stay off `avoidCells`. |
| `path(g, points, opts)` | `path(g, [[3,33],[12,38],[21,43]], {width:2, endY:deckY})` | Follows the ground. Steps are smoothed to at most 1 by cutting or filling, each rise gets a stair facing up the slope (`stairs` "cobblestone"), headroom is cleared, and the surface is `material` ("dirt_path"). `startY`/`endY` pin the ends to meet a bridge deck or a door. |
| `bridge(g, from, to, opts)` | `bridge(g, [21,14,43], [31,14,43], {width:3})` | A deck (`spruce_planks`) on log beams, `parapet` fences along both sides, and `abutment` rock under the ends down to the ground. |

`groundAt(g, x, z)` gives the top ground block of a column (ignoring plants, leaves, logs and water); use it to
stand things on the terrain.

## Water that works when placed

Still reaches are source blocks only, and `containWater` (run by both water brushes) seals every water cell's
open sides and underside, so nothing spreads when the structure is placed. A fall is written in the state the
game settles into: lip source, then a level-1 cell over the edge, then level-8 falling cells, then pool sources.
On placement the game recomputes the same blocks. The renderer draws water translucent, with source surfaces at

Identity: a rough-stone Norman/Burgundy farmhouse with a steep red-tile roof and a brick chimney, a timber lean-to porch on its garden side,
and beside it a walled, symmetrical potager with raised beds, a well at the crossing of its paths, trained fruit trees on the walls,
a glasshouse, a cold frame and a tool shed. Site 40 (x) by 36 (z) by 18 (y). Front = NORTH (-z), the street is at z<0.

# Plan: suburban McMansion on a cul-de-sac lot

Identity: a 2-storey-plus-attic builder-grade McMansion: jumbled dark-asphalt roofs (tall front gable over a two-storey columned portico, hips over a 3-car garage wing and a family-room wing, a conical turret bay), stone veneer on the lower front, beige siding above, white trim and quoins, black shutters. Front = NORTH (-z); street at z<0 side. Grid 44 (x 0..43) x 15 (y 0..14) x 32 (z 0..31). Ground block layer y=0 (grass); walking surface y=1. All ranges inclusive. `runParts` rule: a later part only ADDS into air, so P1/P2 leave every opening, void and RESERVED cell empty.

Workers: read vocab.mjs (constants SITE, OPENINGS, ROOMS, helpers below) then only your own part.

## SITE (block coordinates)
| mass / feature | x | y | z | notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ground | 0..43 | 0 | 0..31 | `grass_block` everywhere first (P1); other parts overwrite their own footprints (ground stays writable) |
| main block M | 18..35 | 0..9 | 11..25 | walls y1..9 outer ring x18/x35/z11/z25; floor y0; 2nd floor slab y5; ceiling/top plate y9; inner x19..34 z12..24 |
| east family wing W | 35..42 | 0..9 | 12..24 | shares wall x=35 with M; inner x36..41 z13..23; wall z=12 front, z=24 back, x=42 east |
| turret bay T | 38..42 | 0..9 | 8..12 | chamfer: cells (38,8) and (42,8) NOT built; inner x39..41 z9..11; shares z=12 wall row with W |
| garage wing G | 1..17 | 0..9 | 7..24 | east wall x=17 (touches M's x=18 wall); inner x2..16 z8..23; front wall z=7, back z=24 |
| portico | 22..31 | 0..9 | 7..10 | EMPTY in P1 (RESERVED), built by P4; gable roof over it by P3 |
| entry gable roof | 22..31 | 10..14 | 7..18 | cross-gable ridge along z, ridge top y=14 |
| main hip roof | 17..36 | 10..13 | 10..26 | rect walls [18,11,35,25] + overhang 1; ridge y=13 |
| wing hip roof | 34..43 | 10..12 | 11..25 | rect walls [35,12,42,24]; ridge y=12 |
| garage hip roof | 0..18 | 10..12 | 6..25 | rect walls [1,7,17,24]; ridge y=12 |
| turret cone | 37..43 | 10..14 | 7..13 | cone over rect [38,8,42,12], base y=10, finial y=14 |
| chimney | 39..41 | 1..14 | 25..26 | RESERVED outside the wing's back wall z=24; fireplace inside at z=23 |
| back deck | 19..34 | 1..2 | 26..31 | planks at y=1 (walk y=2), railing y=2 |
| street | 0..43 | 0 | 0 | `gray_concrete`; curb z=1 `polished_andesite`; sidewalk z=2 `smooth_stone` |
| driveway | 2..17 | 0 | 2..6 | `light_gray_concrete` (replaces sidewalk at x2..17) |
| front lawn | 18..43 | 0 | 3..6 | grass; front walk x26..27 z3..6; east lawn x36..43 z3..7 |
| young tree | 34..38 | 1..7 | 3..7 | trunk (36,1..4,5) |

Top of build: tree y<=7, turret finial y=14, chimney y=14, entry gable ridge y=14. Nothing above y=14.

Floors: floor-1 walking y=1 (block at y=0), floor-2 walking y=6 (block at y=5), top plate y=9, roof from y=10. Rooms: ground air y=1..4, upper air y=6..8, foyer air y=1..8.

## PALETTE (all ids checked with `mcd blocks --check`)
| role | blocks | where |
|---|---|---|
| siding (~40%) | `birch_planks` (+`birch_slab`, `birch_stairs`) | all walls above y=4 and non-front walls |
| stone veneer (~15%) | per-cell hash `andesite` 40 / `stone` 30 / `cobblestone` 20 / `stone_bricks` 10; `stone_brick_stairs/slab/wall`, `andesite_stairs/slab/wall` | y1..4 of north faces (z=7 G, z=11 M, z=12 W, all T faces, wrap 3 cells round corners x=1/x=17/x=18); plinth y=0 under walls `stone_bricks` |
| white trim (~10%) | `quartz_block`, `smooth_quartz` (+`_stairs`, `_slab`), `quartz_pillar`, `chiseled_quartz_block` | belt course row y=5 and frieze row y=9 on exterior wall planes (`smooth_quartz`), quoins, sills, hoods, columns |
| roof (~25%) | palette `dark-slate` (`deepslate_tiles`, `cobbled_deepslate`, `blackstone` + stairs/slabs), ridge `deepslate_tile_slab` | all roofs |
| shutters/accents | `black_concrete` (flush shutter strips), `dark_oak_trapdoor`, `dark_oak_door`, `dark_oak_planks`, `blackstone_wall`, `iron_bars`, `lantern` | beside windows, doors, lamps |
| doors/glass | `glass_pane`, `white_concrete`, `dark_oak_door` | |
| ground | `grass_block`, `coarse_dirt` (mulch), `light_gray_concrete` (drive), `gray_concrete`, `polished_andesite`, `smooth_stone`, `stone`, `stone_bricks`, `stone_brick_slab` | |
| plants | `azalea_leaves`, `flowering_azalea_leaves`, `oak_log`, `oak_leaves` (all `persistent=true`), `short_grass`, `poppy`, `allium`, `peony`, `rose_bush`, `lilac`, `white_tulip` | |
| deck | `spruce_planks`, `spruce_log`, `spruce_fence`, `spruce_stairs`, `spruce_slab` | |
| interior structure | partitions `white_concrete`, stair `oak_stairs`, stair fill `oak_planks`, ladder none | |
Contrast: black/slate roof vs beige siding vs white trim vs grey stone vs black shutters.

Floor material per room (laid by the part that builds the shell): foyer checker `quartz_block`/`black_concrete` (cell (x+z) even = quartz); office, dining `dark_oak_planks`; kitchen, family, bay nook, passages, gallery, BR2-4, primary, closet `oak_planks`; bath `smooth_quartz`; garage `light_gray_concrete`; mudroom `stone_bricks`; bonus `spruce_planks`. The y=5 slab layer carries the upper room floors; the same layer is the ceiling under them.

## VOCABULARY (helpers in vocab.mjs)
- `wallBlock(face,x,y,z)`: y=0 `stone_bricks`; y5 and y9 on exterior planes `smooth_quartz`; north-facing wall plane (see PALETTE) y1..4 veneer hash; else `birch_planks`. `quoins`: at corner columns (1,7),(17,7),(18,11),(1,24),(17,24),(18,25),(35,25),(42,24): corner cell y1..9 `quartz_block`; the neighbour cell along each exposed face is `quartz_block` when y is even, siding when odd (skip y=5, y=9 which are already bands). `shutterCells`: for every window in OPENINGS flagged `sh`, wall cells at x0-1 and x1+1 (or z0-1, z1+1 on x-faces) over the window's y-range are `black_concrete`.
- `archWindow(x0,x1,yb,yt,plane,face)` (P4): fill the opening with `glass_pane`; top row corner cells x0 and x1 at yt become `quartz_stairs` half=top, facing = away from the window centre (x0: west, x1: east) so they read as arch springers; if the window is 1 wide put `quartz_slab` type=top at yt instead of a pane; sill = row of `quartz_slab` type=top on the outside plane (plane-1 for north faces) at y=yb-1 across x0..x1; hood = row of `quartz_slab` type=bottom on the outside plane at y=yt+1.
- `entryDoor` (P4): opening x25..28 y1..4 at z=11. `dark_oak_door` x26 and x27, y1..2, facing north, hinges outward (x26 hinge=right? verify with `mcd states dark_oak_door` and a render so the pair meets in the middle), sidelights `glass_pane` x25 and x28 y1..3, transom row y=3 x26,x27 `glass_pane`, fan row y=4 x26,x27 `glass_pane`, springers `quartz_stairs` half=top at (25,4) facing west and (28,4) facing east; a `quartz_slab` type=top threshold at y=0? (skip, flush). Upper palladian: opening x25..28 y6..8 at z=11: pane fill, arch springers at (25,8) west and (28,8) east, mullions `quartz_block` at (26,6..7)? no: one centre mullion column x=27 y6..7 `quartz_pillar`? keep: mullions at x=26 and x=27 `glass_pane` (no mullion).
- `column(x,z)` (P4): `quartz_slab` type=bottom y=1 base, `quartz_pillar` axis=y y=2..7, `chiseled_quartz_block` y=8 capital; above y=9 the entablature.
- `portico()` (P4): floor y=0 x22..31 z7..10 `stone_bricks`; centre inlay `smooth_quartz` x26..27 z7..10; columns at (23,7),(25,7),(28,7),(30,7) and half columns flush to wall at (23,10),(30,10) (quartz_pillar y1..8); entablature `quartz_block` row y=9 x22..31 at z=7; side beams y=9 at x22 and x31, z=7..10; ceiling `birch_planks` y=9 x23..30 z8..10; landing `stone_brick_slab` type=bottom y=1 x24..29 z=6; two `lantern` standing on `quartz_slab` at (24,2,10) and (29,2,10)? skip: one hanging `lantern` (hanging=true) at (26,8,8) and (27,8,8) from `iron_chain` y=9? no ceiling is y=9: lantern y=8 hanging=true under ceiling block.
- `carriageDoor(x0)` (P4): opening x0..x0+3 y1..3 at z=7: y1..2 all four cells `white_concrete`; `dark_oak_trapdoor` open=true half=bottom facing=north at (x0+1,1,6),(x0+2,1,6),(x0+1,2,6),(x0+2,2,6) as raised bracing (check state vs render); y=3 row: x0 and x0+3 `white_concrete`, x0+1 and x0+2 `glass_pane`; header `dark_oak_planks` row y=4 x0..x0+3 on the outside plane z=6 under... NO: header is the wall cell row y=4 which P2 builds as veneer; instead add a `quartz_slab` type=bottom hood on the outside plane z=6 at y=4.
- `lampPost(x,z)` (P4/P5): `blackstone_wall` y=1..3, `lantern` y=4 (hanging=false).
- `shrub(x,z)` (P5): `azalea_leaves` persistent 3 wide x 1 deep x 2 high (y=1..2) on `coarse_dirt` mulch at y=0 (mulch strip 1 wider all round); every third shrub `flowering_azalea_leaves` at the top centre.
- `youngTree` (P5): `oak_log` axis=y (36,1..4,5); `oak_leaves` persistent=true: layer y=4 and y=5 radius 2 (drop the 4 corner cells), layer y=6 radius 1, y=7 centre; `oak_fence` stake (35,1,5) and (37,1,5), `coarse_dirt` mulch ring at y=0 radius 1.
- `deck()` (P6): see Part 6.
- `chimney()` (P3): footprint x39..41 z25..26. y1..2 base ring `stone_bricks` with `stone_brick_stairs` shoulders; shaft y3..13 `stone_bricks` with `andesite` courses at y=6 and y=10; cap y=14: `stone_brick_slab` type=top over the whole footprint, two pots (40,14,25) `stone_brick_wall`? keep: wall pillars at (39,14,25) and (41,14,25) (pots), no more.
- `roofSpec` (P3), for `$MCD roof` / `roof()` (house -> preset `cottage` as the base, overridden to hip/gable and the dark-slate palette, as below). Order inside P3: entry gable, main hip, wing hip, garage hip, turret cone, chimney last (may overwrite roof cells only inside x39..41 z25..26):

  2. main hip: [[18,11,35,25]] hip, y=10, pitch 0.55, maxHeight 4, overhang 1, eave cornice, ridge slab, dark-slate, dormers: south slope x=21 and x=31, north slope x=20 (west of gable).
  3. wing hip: [[35,12,42,24]] hip, y=10, pitch 0.5, maxHeight 3, dark-slate, dormer north slope x=39.
  4. garage hip: [[1,7,17,24]] hip, y=10, pitch 0.5, maxHeight 3, dark-slate, dormers north slope x=4 and x=13.

All ranges inclusive. `runParts` rule: a later part only ADDS into air, so P1/P2 leave every opening, void and RESERVED cell empty.

# Plan: suburban McMansion on a cul-de-sac lot

Identity: a 2-storey-plus-attic builder-grade McMansion: jumbled dark-asphalt roofs (tall front gable over a two-storey columned portico, hips over a 3-car garage wing and a family-room wing, a conical turret bay), stone veneer on the lower front, beige siding above, white trim and quoins, black shutters. Front = NORTH (-z); street at z<0 side. Grid 44 (x 0..43) x 15 (y 0..14) x 32 (z 0..31). Ground block layer y=0 (grass); walking surface y=1. All ranges inclusive. `runParts` rule: a later part only ADDS into air, so P1/P2 leave every opening, void and RESERVED cell empty.

Workers: read vocab.mjs (constants SITE, OPENINGS, ROOMS, helpers below) then only your own part.

## SITE (block coordinates)

# Plan: suburban McMansion on a cul-de-sac lot

Identity: a 2-storey-plus-attic builder-grade McMansion: jumbled dark-asphalt roofs (tall front gable over a two-storey columned portico, hips over a 3-car garage wing and a family-room wing, a conical turret bay), stone veneer on the lower front, beige siding above, white trim and quoins, black shutters. Front = NORTH (-z); street at z<0 side. Grid 44 (x 0..43) x 15 (y 0..14) x 32 (z 0..31). Ground block layer y=0 (grass); walking surface y=1. All ranges inclusive. `runParts` rule: a later part only ADDS into air, so P1/P2 leave every opening, void and RESERVED cell empty.

Workers: read vocab.mjs (constants SITE, OPENINGS, ROOMS, helpers below) then only your own part.

## SITE (block coordinates)
| mass / feature | x | y | z | notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ground | 0..43 | 0 | 0..31 | `grass_block` everywhere first (P1); other parts overwrite their own footprints (ground stays writable) |
| main block M | 18..35 | 0..9 | 11..25 | walls y1..9 outer ring x18/x35/z11/z25; floor y0; 2nd floor slab y5; ceiling/top plate y9; inner x19..34 z12..24 |
| east family wing W | 35..42 | 0..9 | 12..24 | shares wall x=35 with M; inner x36..41 z13..23; wall z=12 front, z=24 back, x=42 east |
| turret bay T | 38..42 | 0..9 | 8..12 | chamfer: cells (38,8) and (42,8) NOT built; inner x39..41 z9..11; shares z=12 wall row with W |
| garage wing G | 1..17 | 0..9 | 7..24 | east wall x=17 (touches M's x=18 wall); inner x2..16 z8..23; front wall z=7, back z=24 |
| portico | 22..31 | 0..9 | 7..10 | EMPTY in P1 (RESERVED), built by P4; gable roof over it by P3 |
| entry gable roof | 22..31 | 10..14 | 7..18 | cross-gable ridge along z, ridge top y=14 |
| main hip roof | 17..36 | 10..13 | 10..26 | rect walls [18,11,35,25] + overhang 1; ridge y=13 |
| wing hip roof | 34..43 | 10..12 | 11..25 | rect walls [35,12,42,24]; ridge y=12 |
| garage hip roof | 0..18 | 10..12 | 6..25 | rect walls [1,7,17,24]; ridge y=12 |
| turret cone | 37..43 | 10..14 | 7..13 | cone over rect [38,8,42,12], base y=10, finial y=14 |
| chimney | 39..41 | 1..14 | 25..26 | RESERVED outside the wing's back wall z=24; fireplace inside at z=23 |
| back deck | 19..34 | 1..2 | 26..31 | planks at y=1 (walk y=2), railing y=2 |
| street | 0..43 | 0 | 0 | `gray_concrete`; curb z=1 `polished_andesite`; sidewalk z=2 `smooth_stone` |
| driveway | 2..17 | 0 | 2..6 | `light_gray_concrete` (replaces sidewalk at x2..17) |
| front lawn | 18..43 | 0 | 3..6 | grass; front walk x26..27 z3..6; east lawn x36..43 z3..7 |
| young tree | 34..38 | 1..7 | 3..7 | trunk (36,1..4,5) |

Top of build: tree y<=7, turret finial y=14, chimney y=14, entry gable ridge y=14. Nothing above y=14.

Floors: floor-1 walking y=1 (block at y=0), floor-2 walking y=6 (block at y=5), top plate y=9, roof from y=10. Rooms: ground air y=1..4, upper air y=6..8, foyer air y=1..8.

## PALETTE (all ids checked with `mcd blocks --check`)
| role | blocks | where |
|---|---|---|
| siding (~40%) | `birch_planks` (+`birch_slab`, `birch_stairs`) | all walls above y=4 and non-front walls |
| stone veneer (~15%) | per-cell hash `andesite` 40 / `stone` 30 / `cobblestone` 20 / `stone_bricks` 10; `stone_brick_stairs/slab/wall`, `andesite_stairs/slab/wall` | y1..4 of north faces (z=7 G, z=11 M, z=12 W, all T faces, wrap 3 cells round corners x=1/x=17/x=18); plinth y=0 under walls `stone_bricks` |
| white trim (~10%) | `quartz_block`, `smooth_quartz` (+`_stairs`, `_slab`), `quartz_pillar`, `chiseled_quartz_block` | belt course row y=5 and frieze row y=9 on exterior wall planes (`smooth_quartz`), quoins, sills, hoods, columns |
| roof (~25%) | palette `dark-slate` (`deepslate_tiles`, `cobbled_deepslate`, `blackstone` + stairs/slabs), ridge `deepslate_tile_slab` | all roofs |

| doors/glass | `glass_pane`, `white_concrete`, `dark_oak_door` | |
| ground | `grass_block`, `coarse_dirt` (mulch), `light_gray_concrete` (drive), `gray_concrete`, `polished_andesite`, `smooth_stone`, `stone`, `stone_bricks`, `stone_brick_slab` | |
| plants | `azalea_leaves`, `flowering_azalea_leaves`, `oak_log`, `oak_leaves` (all `persistent=true`), `short_grass`, `poppy`, `allium`, `peony`, `rose_bush`, `lilac`, `white_tulip` | |
| deck | `spruce_planks`, `spruce_log`, `spruce_fence`, `spruce_stairs`, `spruce_slab` | |
| interior structure | partitions `white_concrete`, stair `oak_stairs`, stair fill `oak_planks`, ladder none | |
Contrast: black/slate roof vs beige siding vs white trim vs grey stone vs black shutters.

Floor material per room (laid by the part that builds the shell): foyer checker `quartz_block`/`black_concrete` (cell (x+z) even = quartz); office, dining `dark_oak_planks`; kitchen, family, bay nook, passages, gallery, BR2-4, primary, closet `oak_planks`; bath `smooth_quartz`; garage `light_gray_concrete`; mudroom `stone_bricks`; bonus `spruce_planks`. The y=5 slab layer carries the upper room floors; the same layer is the ceiling under them.

- `archWindow(x0,x1,yb,yt,plane,face)` (P4): fill the opening with `glass_pane`; top row corner cells x0 and x1 at yt become `quartz_stairs` half=top, facing = away from the window centre (x0: west, x1: east) so they read as arch springers; if the window is 1 wide put `quartz_slab` type=top at yt instead of a pane; sill = row of `quartz_slab` type=top on the outside plane (plane-1 for north faces) at y=yb-1 across x0..x1; hood = row of `quartz_slab` type=bottom on the outside plane at y=yt+1.

Palladian window above: opening x25..28 y6..8 at z=11: `glass_pane` fill, springers `quartz_stairs` half=top at (25,8) facing west and (28,8) facing east, sill and hood as `archWindow`.
- `column(x,z)` (P4): `quartz_slab` type=bottom y=1 base, `quartz_pillar` axis=y y=2..7, `chiseled_quartz_block` y=8 capital; above y=9 the entablature.
- `portico()` (P4): floor y=0 x22..31 z7..10 `stone_bricks`; centre inlay `smooth_quartz` x26..27 z7..10; columns at (23,7),(25,7),(28,7),(30,7) and half columns flush to wall at (23,10),(30,10) (quartz_pillar y1..8); entablature `quartz_block` row y=9 x22..31 at z=7; side beams y=9 at x22 and x31, z=7..10; ceiling `birch_planks` y=9 x23..30 z8..10; landing `stone_brick_slab` type=bottom y=1 x24..29 z=6; two hanging `lantern` (hanging=true) at (26,8,8) and (27,8,8) under the y=9 ceiling.
- `carriageDoor(x0)` (P4): opening x0..x0+3 y1..3 at z=7: y1..2 all four cells `white_concrete`; `dark_oak_trapdoor` open=true half=bottom facing=north at (x0+1,1,6),(x0+2,1,6),(x0+1,2,6),(x0+2,2,6) as raised bracing (check state vs render); y=3 row: x0 and x0+3 `white_concrete`, x0+1 and x0+2 `glass_pane`; the wall row y=4 above is veneer (built by P2); add a `quartz_slab` type=bottom hood on the outside plane z=6 at y=4 across x0..x0+3.
- `lampPost(x,z)` (P4/P5): `blackstone_wall` y=1..3, `lantern` y=4 (hanging=false).

- `deck()` (P6): see Part 6.

# Plan: suburban McMansion on a cul-de-sac lot

Identity: a 2-storey-plus-attic builder-grade McMansion: jumbled dark-asphalt roofs (tall front gable over a two-storey columned portico, hips over a 3-car garage wing and a family-room wing, a conical turret bay), stone veneer on the lower front, beige siding above, white trim and quoins, black shutters. Front = NORTH (-z); street at z<0 side. Grid 44 (x 0..43) x 15 (y 0..14) x 32 (z 0..31). Ground block layer y=0 (grass); walking surface y=1. All ranges inclusive. `runParts` rule: a later part only ADDS into air, so P1/P2 leave every opening, void and RESERVED cell empty.

Workers: read vocab.mjs (constants SITE, OPENINGS, ROOMS, helpers below) then only your own part.

## SITE (block coordinates)
| mass / feature | x | y | z | notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ground | 0..43 | 0 | 0..31 | `grass_block` everywhere first (P1); other parts overwrite their own footprints (ground stays writable) |
| main block M | 18..35 | 0..9 | 11..25 | walls y1..9 outer ring x18/x35/z11/z25; floor y0; 2nd floor slab y5; ceiling/top plate y9; inner x19..34 z12..24 |
| east family wing W | 35..42 | 0..9 | 12..24 | shares wall x=35 with M; inner x36..41 z13..23; wall z=12 front, z=24 back, x=42 east |
| turret bay T | 38..42 | 0..9 | 8..12 | chamfer: cells (38,8) and (42,8) NOT built; inner x39..41 z9..11; shares z=12 wall row with W |
| garage wing G | 1..17 | 0..9 | 7..24 | east wall x=17 (touches M's x=18 wall); inner x2..16 z8..23; front wall z=7, back z=24 |
| portico | 22..31 | 0..9 | 7..10 | EMPTY in P1 (RESERVED), built by P4; gable roof over it by P3 |
| entry gable roof | 22..31 | 10..14 | 7..18 | cross-gable ridge along z, ridge top y=14 |
| main hip roof | 17..36 | 10..13 | 10..26 | rect walls [18,11,35,25] + overhang 1; ridge y=13 |
| wing hip roof | 34..43 | 10..12 | 11..25 | rect walls [35,12,42,24]; ridge y=12 |
| garage hip roof | 0..18 | 10..12 | 6..25 | rect walls [1,7,17,24]; ridge y=12 |
| turret cone | 37..43 | 10..14 | 7..13 | cone over rect [38,8,42,12], base y=10, finial y=14 |
| chimney | 39..41 | 1..14 | 25..26 | RESERVED outside the wing's back wall z=24; fireplace inside at z=23 |
| back deck | 19..34 | 1..2 | 26..31 | planks at y=1 (walk y=2), railing y=2 |
| street | 0..43 | 0 | 0 | `gray_concrete`; curb z=1 `polished_andesite`; sidewalk z=2 `smooth_stone` |
| driveway | 2..17 | 0 | 2..6 | `light_gray_concrete` (replaces sidewalk at x2..17) |
| front lawn | 18..43 | 0 | 3..6 | grass; front walk x26..27 z3..6; east lawn x36..43 z3..7 |
| young tree | 34..38 | 1..7 | 3..7 | trunk (36,1..4,5) |

Top of build: tree y<=7, turret finial y=14, chimney y=14, entry gable ridge y=14. Nothing above y=14.

Floors: floor-1 walking y=1 (block at y=0), floor-2 walking y=6 (block at y=5), top plate y=9, roof from y=10. Rooms: ground air y=1..4, upper air y=6..8, foyer air y=1..8.

## PALETTE (all ids checked with `mcd blocks --check`)
| role | blocks | where |
|---|---|---|
| siding (~40%) | `birch_planks` (+`birch_slab`, `birch_stairs`) | all walls above y=4 and non-front walls |
| stone veneer (~15%) | per-cell hash `andesite` 40 / `stone` 30 / `cobblestone` 20 / `stone_bricks` 10; `stone_brick_stairs/slab/wall`, `andesite_stairs/slab/wall` | y1..4 of north faces (z=7 G, z=11 M, z=12 W, all T faces, wrap 3 cells round corners x=1/x=17/x=18); plinth y=0 under walls `stone_bricks` |
| white trim (~10%) | `quartz_block`, `smooth_quartz` (+`_stairs`, `_slab`), `quartz_pillar`, `chiseled_quartz_block` | belt course row y=5 and frieze row y=9 on exterior wall planes (`smooth_quartz`), quoins, sills, hoods, columns |
| roof (~25%) | palette `dark-slate` (`deepslate_tiles`, `cobbled_deepslate`, `blackstone` + stairs/slabs), ridge `deepslate_tile_slab` | all roofs |
| shutters/accents | `black_concrete` (flush shutter strips), `dark_oak_trapdoor`, `dark_oak_door`, `dark_oak_planks`, `blackstone_wall`, `iron_bars`, `lantern` | beside windows, doors, lamps |
| doors/glass | `glass_pane`, `white_concrete`, `dark_oak_door` | |
| ground | `grass_block`, `coarse_dirt` (mulch), `light_gray_concrete` (drive), `gray_concrete`, `polished_andesite`, `smooth_stone`, `stone`, `stone_bricks`, `stone_brick_slab` | |
| plants | `azalea_leaves`, `flowering_azalea_leaves`, `oak_log`, `oak_leaves` (all `persistent=true`), `short_grass`, `poppy`, `allium`, `peony`, `rose_bush`, `lilac`, `white_tulip` | |
| deck | `spruce_planks`, `spruce_log`, `spruce_fence`, `spruce_stairs`, `spruce_slab` | |
| interior structure | partitions `white_concrete`, stair `oak_stairs`, stair fill `oak_planks`, ladder none | |
Contrast: black/slate roof vs beige siding vs white trim vs grey stone vs black shutters.

Floor material per room (laid by the part that builds the shell): foyer checker `quartz_block`/`black_concrete` (cell (x+z) even = quartz); office, dining `dark_oak_planks`; kitchen, family, bay nook, passages, gallery, BR2-4, primary, closet `oak_planks`; bath `smooth_quartz`; garage `light_gray_concrete`; mudroom `stone_bricks`; bonus `spruce_planks`. The y=5 slab layer carries the upper room floors; the same layer is the ceiling under them.

## VOCABULARY (helpers in vocab.mjs)
- `wallBlock(face,x,y,z)`: y=0 `stone_bricks`; y5 and y9 on exterior planes `smooth_quartz`; north-facing wall plane (see PALETTE) y1..4 veneer hash; else `birch_planks`. `quoins`: at corner columns (1,7),(17,7),(18,11),(1,24),(17,24),(18,25),(35,25),(42,24): corner cell y1..9 `quartz_block`; the neighbour cell along each exposed face is `quartz_block` when y is even, siding when odd (skip y=5, y=9 which are already bands). `shutterCells`: for every window in OPENINGS flagged `sh`, wall cells at x0-1 and x1+1 (or z0-1, z1+1 on x-faces) over the window's y-range are `black_concrete`.
- `archWindow(x0,x1,yb,yt,plane,face)` (P4): fill the opening with `glass_pane`; top row corner cells x0 and x1 at yt become `quartz_stairs` half=top, facing = away from the window centre (x0: west, x1: east) so they read as arch springers; if the window is 1 wide put `quartz_slab` type=top at yt instead of a pane; sill = row of `quartz_slab` type=top on the outside plane (plane-1 for north faces) at y=yb-1 across x0..x1; hood = row of `quartz_slab` type=bottom on the outside plane at y=yt+1.
- `entryDoor` (P4): opening x25..28 y1..4 at z=11. `dark_oak_door` at x26 and x27, y1..2 (lower+upper half), facing north, hinges on the outer ends so the pair meets in the middle (check `mcd states dark_oak_door` and a render), sidelights `glass_pane` x25 and x28 y1..3, transom row y=3 x26,x27 `glass_pane`, fan row y=4 x26,x27 `glass_pane`, springers `quartz_stairs` half=top at (25,4) facing west and (28,4) facing east. Palladian window above: opening x25..28 y6..8 at z=11: `glass_pane` fill, springers `quartz_stairs` half=top at (25,8) facing west and (28,8) facing east, sill and hood as `archWindow`.
- `column(x,z)` (P4): `quartz_slab` type=bottom y=1 base, `quartz_pillar` axis=y y=2..7, `chiseled_quartz_block` y=8 capital; above y=9 the entablature.
- `portico()` (P4): floor y=0 x22..31 z7..10 `stone_bricks`; centre inlay `smooth_quartz` x26..27 z7..10; columns at (23,7),(25,7),(28,7),(30,7) and half columns flush to wall at (23,10),(30,10) (quartz_pillar y1..8); entablature `quartz_block` row y=9 x22..31 at z=7; side beams y=9 at x22 and x31, z=7..10; ceiling `birch_planks` y=9 x23..30 z8..10; landing `stone_brick_slab` type=bottom y=1 x24..29 z=6; two hanging `lantern` (hanging=true) at (26,8,8) and (27,8,8) under the y=9 ceiling.
- `carriageDoor(x0)` (P4): opening x0..x0+3 y1..3 at z=7: y1..2 all four cells `white_concrete`; `dark_oak_trapdoor` open=true half=bottom facing=north at (x0+1,1,6),(x0+2,1,6),(x0+1,2,6),(x0+2,2,6) as raised bracing (check state vs render); y=3 row: x0 and x0+3 `white_concrete`, x0+1 and x0+2 `glass_pane`; the wall row y=4 above is veneer (built by P2); add a `quartz_slab` type=bottom hood on the outside plane z=6 at y=4 across x0..x0+3.
- `lampPost(x,z)` (P4/P5): `blackstone_wall` y=1..3, `lantern` y=4 (hanging=false).
- `shrub(x,z)` (P5): `azalea_leaves` persistent 3 wide x 1 deep x 2 high (y=1..2) on `coarse_dirt` mulch at y=0 (mulch strip 1 wider all round); every third shrub `flowering_azalea_leaves` at the top centre.
- `youngTree` (P5): `oak_log` axis=y (36,1..4,5); `oak_leaves` persistent=true: layer y=4 and y=5 radius 2 (drop the 4 corner cells), layer y=6 radius 1, y=7 centre; `oak_fence` stake (35,1,5) and (37,1,5), `coarse_dirt` mulch ring at y=0 radius 1.
- `deck()` (P6): see Part 6.
- `chimney()` (P3): footprint x39..41 z25..26. y1..2 base ring `stone_bricks` with `stone_brick_stairs` shoulders; shaft y3..13 `stone_bricks` with `andesite` courses at y=6 and y=10; cap y=14: `stone_brick_slab` type=top over the whole footprint, plus two pots: `stone_brick_wall` at (39,14,25) and (41,14,25) (stacked above the slab, so those two cells are the wall instead of the slab).
- `roofSpec` (P3), for `$MCD roof` / `roof()` (house -> preset `cottage` as the base, overridden to hip/gable and the dark-slate palette, as below). Order inside P3: entry gable, main hip, wing hip, garage hip, turret cone, chimney last (may overwrite roof cells only inside x39..41 z25..26):
  1. entry gable: rects [[22,7,31,18]] style gable, y=10, pitch 1.0, maxHeight 5, ridge along z, overhang 1, eave cornice, wall fill `birch_planks`, verge `quartz_stairs`, material dark-slate, round vent 2x2 `glass_pane` at (26..27, 11..12, 7) framed by `quartz_block`.
  2. main hip: [[18,11,35,25]] hip, y=10, pitch 0.55, maxHeight 4, overhang 1, eave cornice, ridge slab, dark-slate, dormers: south slope x=21 and x=31, north slope x=20 (west of gable).
  3. wing hip: [[35,12,42,24]] hip, y=10, pitch 0.5, maxHeight 3, dark-slate, dormer north slope x=39.
  4. garage hip: [[1,7,17,24]] hip, y=10, pitch 0.5, maxHeight 3, dark-slate, dormers north slope x=4 and x=13.
  5. turret: [[38,8,42,12]] preset `tower-cap` (cone, flare, finial `lightning_rod` at y=14), material dark-slate.
  Use `--no-contrast` NOT needed; roof dark-slate vs beige siding passes. Check `ROOF_BIG_PLANE` and fix with the dormers.

## ROOMS
Walking y=1 (ground) / y=6 (upper). Boxes are inner air [x0,y0,z0,x1,y1,z1]. Floor material per room above.
| room | box | purpose / mood | ways in |
|---|---|---|---|

# Plan: suburban McMansion on a cul-de-sac lot

Identity: a 2-storey-plus-attic builder-grade McMansion: jumbled dark-asphalt roofs (tall front gable over a two-storey columned portico, hips over a 3-car garage wing and a family-room wing, a conical turret bay), stone veneer on the lower front, beige siding above, white trim and quoins, black shutters. Front = NORTH (-z); street at z<0 side. Grid 44 (x 0..43) x 15 (y 0..14) x 32 (z 0..31). Ground block layer y=0 (grass); walking surface y=1. All ranges inclusive. `runParts` rule: a later part only ADDS into air, so P1/P2 leave every opening, void and RESERVED cell empty.

Workers: read vocab.mjs (constants SITE, OPENINGS, ROOMS, helpers below) then only your own part.

# Plan: suburban McMansion on a cul-de-sac lot

Identity: a 2-storey-plus-attic builder-grade McMansion: jumbled dark-asphalt roofs (tall front gable over a two-storey columned portico, hips over a 3-car garage wing and a family-room wing, a conical turret bay), stone veneer on the lower front, beige siding above, white trim and quoins, black shutters. Front = NORTH (-z); street at z<0 side. Grid 44 (x 0..43) x 15 (y 0..14) x 32 (z 0..31). Ground block layer y=0 (grass); walking surface y=1. All ranges inclusive. `runParts` rule: a later part only ADDS into air, so P1/P2 leave every opening, void and RESERVED cell empty.

Workers: read vocab.mjs (constants SITE, OPENINGS, ROOMS, helpers below) then only your own part.

## SITE (block coordinates)

Palladian window above: opening x25..28 y6..8 at z=11: `glass_pane` fill, springers `quartz_stairs` half=top at (25,8) facing west and (28,8) facing east, sill and hood as `archWindow`.

input.concept_subject: A suburban McMansion seen from the cul-de-sac street, front facing the viewer. On the left, a wide three-car garage wing with three white carriage-style doors (small window panes along their tops), black-shuttered windows of a bonus room above, and a hipped dark asphalt-shingle roof with two dormers. Beyond it, in the middle, a two-storey beige-sided main block under a tall steep front gable in dark slate shingles. Below the gable, a double-height white portico with four tall quartz columns, a fanlighted double door with sidelights, and a big arched palladian window above it. Left of the portico, a small gabled dormer on the main roof. To the right, a hipped family wing whose front corner is a round-ish turret bay with a conical dark-slate cap and a thin finial, tall narrow arched windows, a big stone chimney on its back. The lower storey of the front is grey stone veneer (andesite, stone, cobblestone mix), with beige siding above, a white belt course between the storeys, white quoins at the corners, white window sills and hoods, and black shutters on the tall arched windows. A wide light-grey concrete driveway runs to the garage, with a stone-brick front walk to the portico, carriage lamp posts, a mailbox, a manicured lawn with rounded azalea shrubs and flower strips along the foundation, and a young oak with a stake on the right lawn. Behind, a spruce back deck with a railing. 44 wide, 32 deep, 14 tall.

structured_output.concept_subject: A suburban McMansion seen from the cul-de-sac street, front facing the viewer. On the left, a wide three-car garage wing with three white carriage-style doors (small window panes along their tops), black-shuttered windows of a bonus room above, and a hipped dark asphalt-shingle roof with two dormers. Beyond it, in the middle, a two-storey beige-sided main block under a tall steep front gable in dark slate shingles. Below the gable, a double-height white portico with four tall quartz columns, a fanlighted double door with sidelights, and a big arched palladian window above it. Left of the portico, a small gabled dormer on the main roof. To the right, a hipped family wing whose front corner is a round-ish turret bay with a conical dark-slate cap and a thin finial, tall narrow arched windows, a big stone chimney on its back. The lower storey of the front is grey stone veneer (andesite, stone, cobblestone mix), with beige siding above, a white belt course between the storeys, white quoins at the corners, white window sills and hoods, and black shutters on the tall arched windows. A wide light-grey concrete driveway runs to the garage, with a stone-brick front walk to the portico, carriage lamp posts, a mailbox, a manicured lawn with rounded azalea shrubs and flower strips along the foundation, and a young oak with a stake on the right lawn. Behind, a spruce back deck with a railing. 44 wide, 32 deep, 14 tall.
